page: Amazon Web Services m5.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor operating at 3.1 GHz, delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU provides a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, alongside instruction set support including AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. Memory allocation is set at 128.0 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage via its 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark outcomes show mid-tier multi-threaded throughput contrasted against constrained single-thread performance. The instance registers average results in multi-core metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 25,371.43, a stress-ng multi-core score of 26,973.99, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,637.0. Memory throughput is consistent with DDR4 configurations, showing 108.25 GB/sec uncached read and 47.62 GB/sec uncached write speeds across large 256MB blocks. Conversely, single-core execution reflects older microarchitecture characteristics, scoring 1,050.0 in Geekbench single-core, 1,281.79 in stress-ng single-core, and weak single-threaded compression benchmarks.

Workload evaluation highlights suitability for distributed backends, intermediate caching, and general compute queues rather than latency-sensitive or storage-heavy pipelines. Application tests demonstrate steady throughput, achieving 25.93 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 20.63 GB/sec in static web serving. While capable of running lightweight LLM inference on small to medium parameter models, larger architectures scale poorly on pure CPU compute. The absence of integrated NVMe drives requires consideration of EBS operational boundaries, positioning the instance for horizontally scaled web servers, batch compilation jobs, and distributed enterprise microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m5.8xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based virtual server powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor. The configuration features 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. It contains no dedicated GPUs or local storage drives, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations indicate standard multi-core compute and memory bandwidth, scoring 25,371.43 on PassMark CPU and handling 25.93 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles. The 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio provides balanced compute density, making it suitable for multi-threaded enterprise applications, static web serving, software build pipelines, and mid-tier backend services.
